description: The one registry of machine-readable codes for Class Evolution, and for the refusal of an action plan by the rules engine. A rejected command returns exactly one code and changes nothing: no row, no revision, no random draw. Fixtures, the persistence check and the game code use these names and no others.

kinds.command_rejection: Returned as the error_code of a rejected client command.
kinds.award_denial: Stored in mastery_award_event.denial_reason. The award event is accepted and records zero points.
kinds.load_failure: Returned when a saved profile cannot be opened as it is. The save is left untouched.
kinds.content_validation: Reported by the catalog validator at build time. No player ever sees it.
kinds.plan_rejection: Returned by the rules engine as the code of a rejected SetActionPlan or CommitActionPlan, beside the text shown to the player (owner decision of 2026-11-11, fixtures CE-29 and CE-30). It does not depend on the feature gate.

codes.meaning: The run is in a phase that does not allow the command. Vocation and build commands are never allowed while run.phase is 'battle'.
The profile has not discovered the vocation (its discovery state is 'hidden' or 'hinted'). The response carries no detail about the vocation.
The hero's eligibility_state is 'guest' or 'locked', so it cannot claim or change vocations.

No route of the vocation's prerequisite is satisfied for this hero, or (ChangeVocation) the hero has not claimed the vocation. error_details.routes lists, per route, each unmet mastery or quest condition; a missing mastery rank is {"op": "MASTERY_AT_LEAST", "vocation_id", "rank", "current_rank"}. PreviewVocation reports the same structure as blocked_by without being rejected.
Every mastery and quest condition of the chosen route is met, but the profile holds fewer of the route's item than the route consumes.
The inherited skills would cost more than the active vocation's inheritance capacity. error_details gives capacity_max, capacity_used and capacity_requested.
The die cannot be equipped by the active vocation.
The skill modifies a die face, and no equipped die of the active vocation has a face it can modify.
The save names a catalog version that is retired or unknown and the migration manifest has no mapping for it. Nothing is substituted and nothing is discarded.
The command's state_revision is not the current revision of the row it targets (hero.revision for hero commands).
The command asks for a second active vocation. A hero has exactly one.

The command_id was already accepted for a different command (another type or other params). This is the shipped engine's behaviour for run commands, carried over. Sending the same command again is not an error: see replay_result.
The profile already holds as many heroes as the roster allows (12 by the owner's decision of 2026-11-11), so no hero can be recruited. error_details carries the limit and the number of heroes.

The encounter was won, but its threat rating is below the minimum for the hero's active vocation at its current rank. Base and challenge points are both zero. The name is kept from v0.1; it means below the threat floor.
The encounter did not end in victory. Base and challenge points are both zero.
A vocation rank needs a threat rating that no available mastery-eligible encounter reaches, so the rank could never be trained.
A vocation could never be unlocked in the wave it is released in: its prerequisite names a vocation of a later wave, or a quest or item whose encounter is not shipped.
The plan names a die the hero has not rolled this activation.
The plan uses the same die for two actions. A die supplies one action per activation.
The rolled face is a blank. A blank cannot be committed as an action.
The rolled face has no legal target at all in the current battle state.
The action names the wrong number of targets: a single-target face needs exactly one, and a self-targeted face takes only its user.
The action names a target that is not a combatant of this battle.
The target is behind a standing front row. A melee action must target the standing front row first.
The target is downed. Only a face with the revival tag may target a downed ally, and nothing may target a downed enemy.
The target is standing but the face may not take it (for example an ally for an attack).
The actions do not fit the hero's schedule: too many actions, the wrong order of categories, or a repeated category.
In resolution order, an action costs more mana than the hero will have when it resolves. No mana is spent and nothing else changes.

replay_result.meaning: A command whose command_id was already accepted, sent again unchanged, returns the result stored for the first acceptance with duplicate set to true. Nothing is written, no revision changes and no random number is drawn. Only accepted commands are stored, so a rejected or failed command can be sent again with the same command_id. The same holds for a trusted event with an identity that was already applied (a mastery award for the same run, encounter, hero and vocation; an item grant with the same grant_id).

merged_codes.reason: Same condition under two names (fixture CE-37 against the stated list).
A missing mastery rank is one kind of unmet prerequisite; the vocation and rank move into error_details (fixture CE-02).
A repeated command id returns the original result, so it is not an error.

check_order.meaning: When several conditions fail at once, the first one in this order is reported.

No CE fixture reuses a command id for a different command; CE-33 and CE-38 cover the unchanged repeat only. The persistence test suite exercises it against the database.
No CE fixture releases a vocation before its prerequisites; the catalog test suite exercises it wave by wave against the vocation catalog.

plan_check_order.meaning: The order in which a plan is checked. The first failing check is reported. The checks up to TARGET_NOT_LEGAL run for each action in the player's order; SCHEDULE_VIOLATION is checked on the whole plan after them; INSUFFICIENT_MANA is checked last, action by action in resolution order.
